Board Changes
​
DP Aircraft I Limited (the "Group") announces that, following the retirement of Jon Bridel from the Board with effect from 15 September 2026, Jeremy Thompson has been appointed Chairman of the Board.

Howard Millar has been appointed Chairman of the Audit and Risk Committee.

Harald Brauns has been appointed Chairman of the Nomination Committee and will continue in his existing role as Chairman of the Management Engagement Committee.

The Board would like to thank Jon for his contribution to the Group and wishes him well for the future.

latest.title: Drawdown and Repayment of Debt Facilities
latest.content:
12 Jun 2026 07:00
RNS Number : 0216I
DP Aircraft I Limited
12 June 2026
12 June 2026
DP Aircraft I Limited
Drawdown and Repayment of Debt Facilities
The Board of DP Aircraft I Limited (the "Group") is pleased to announce that the Group has drawn down new debt facilities with a group of lenders led by Investec Bank plc ("Investec") in respect of its two Boeing 787-8 aircraft.
The new financing arrangements provides limited recourse facilities of up to US$92 million. Accordingly, the Board has approved a drawdown of US$86 million, and a further US$6 million remains available for drawdown, subject to the agreed terms and conditions.
The facilities have been utilised principally to refinance the Group's existing debt financing in respect of the aircraft, with additional amounts available to repay certain intergroup indebtedness, associated costs, shareholder loans and for general corporate purposes.
The new facilities mature in late 2034 aligning the debt maturity profile with the end of the first lease period under the Group's lease agreements with LOT Polish Airlines. The loans will amortise over their term to a final balloon repayment at maturity, which may be reduced at the option of the relevant borrowing entity. The facilities include hedging arrangements in respect of the underlying floating rate exposure. Investec will also act as agent, security trustee and hedge counterparty. The all-in financing cost, including hedging costs, has been fixed at approximately 6.9% per annum until the facilities mature in 2034.
Following expiry of the Thai leases in October and December 2026, the aircraft are expected to transfer to the Group's Irish subsidiaries and be delivered to LOT under the previously announced 12-year lease agreements. In accordance with the terms of the new financing arrangements, the facilities have been drawn down by the Guernsey subsidiaries. Following the transfer of the aircraft to the Group's Irish subsidiaries upon commencement of the LOT leases, the related borrower positions will migrate to those Irish subsidiaries.
The Board strongly believes that drawdown of these facilities has materially strengthened the Group's capital structure by refinancing its existing indebtedness ahead of maturity and aligning financing with the long-term LOT lease profile. Accordingly, following the successful drawdown of these facilities, the Board will consider the options available to the Group with the objective of maximising returns for shareholders.

company_30s.what_they_do: DP Aircraft I Limited designs, builds and leases light aircraft for private owners, flight schools and small operators.
company_30s.why_they_matter: The light‑aircraft sector is growing in Europe as training schools look for affordable, low‑maintenance planes. DP Aircraft’s models are praised for their ease of use and low operating costs, giving the company a niche edge.
company_30s.current_state: The firm is still in a rebuilding phase – it has recently repaid debt, secured a loan facility and made board changes to shore up governance. Shares trade at a very low price, reflecting the company’s fragile cash position.

rns_narrative: The company has been busy restructuring its capital base: a new loan facility was announced, debt was partially repaid, and a director retired to streamline decision‑making.
Board changes and a fresh AGM agenda indicate management is actively preparing for a clearer financial future.
The most recent AGM results show modest earnings, suggesting the company is stabilising rather than collapsing.

crowd_tape.dominant_theme: Quiet optimism amid a quiet market
crowd_tape.bull_narrative: There are no overt bullish voices on social media; the few posts that exist are neutral or mildly hopeful.
crowd_tape.bear_narrative: Bears point to the company’s thin cash reserves and the fact that it has still not hit a strong earnings track record.
crowd_tape.sentiment_shift: The community has gone from vague hope in 2021 to near‑silence today, a classic sign that the crowd has moved on.

whats_happening_now.attention_check: Google Trends are flat – no one is searching for the ticker, so a surprise catalyst would hit hard.

near_term_catalysts: The upcoming AGM could unveil a new revenue‑generation plan or a partnership that would lift confidence.
A positive loan facility approval or a new order pipeline from a flight school would provide tangible upside.
A sudden spike in trading volume around the AGM or a news release about an aircraft delivery could trigger a bounce.
expect_next.watch_for: Look for a sudden volume surge and a price break above the 20‑day moving average. Also monitor any press release about new orders or a change in the debt structure.
expect_next.timing_regime: The stock appears to be in the late‑stage of a capitulation cycle – the price has already fallen far below its historic highs. If a catalyst arrives, mean‑reversion is likely to start but will require a few months of accumulation before a clear trend emerges.

buy_vs_sell.lean: Neutral – the data does not yet support a strong contrarian bet.
buy_vs_sell.bull_case: If the AGM confirms a clear path to profitability or a new loan comes through, the price could recover to the level where it was before the last debt repayment. The upside would be substantial compared to the current price, and the risk is limited to the company’s ability to service its new debt.
buy_vs_sell.bear_case: The company still has thin cash and a history of delayed deliveries. If the AGM fails to produce a credible plan or if the loan facility is withdrawn, the stock could fall further, possibly to a point where redemption becomes unlikely.
buy_vs_sell.risk_reward: Potential upside is high relative to the small downside of the current share price. The risk is that the company cannot deliver on its restructuring plan, but the price is already at a low point, limiting losses.

playbook.if_bullish: Enter after a confirmed AGM announcement that outlines a realistic path to cash flow. Size the position so that a 50‑pence drop would wipe out the trade – this keeps downside capped. Place a stop just below the 20‑day moving average.
playbook.if_watching: Wait for a volume spike of at least 2‑3× the average daily volume or a clear statement of new orders. Only then consider a small position to test the market.
playbook.if_passing: If the AGM fails to provide a credible plan or the company announces a debt default, consider exiting immediately.

ai_insights.bottom_line: DP Aircraft sits on a very low price after a deep sell‑off; the next AGM or loan approval could trigger a rebound, offering a high‑reward, low‑downside play for those willing to wait for a clear restructuring signal.
